title: BusemannFormer: Horospherical Self-Attention for Hyperbolic Graph Transformers
claim: Scoring keys by alignment with a query-chosen boundary direction, rather than by nearness, gives a hierarchy-aware attention that drops into a standard Transformer block.
layout: 2 panels, left geometric disk with zoom inset, right vertical block diagram
description: Two panels. Panel (a), titled 'Distance vs. HSA', shows a Poincaré disk with a gray tree. A query point q has an arrow to an ideal-boundary point v_i. Orange dashed circles mark equal distance, and blue circles are horospheres. A dashed box on the disk is magnified in an inset. In the inset, the orange nearby key k1 lies on the distance circle, and the blue aligned key k2 lies on the horosphere that touches v_i. A legend says 'Distance favors k1' (orange) and 'HSA favors k2' (blue). Panel (b), titled 'BusemannFormer', shows a vertical stack: Input, Spatial norm, a highlighted blue Multi-head HSA block, residual-add circles, Spatial norm, Feed-forward, then Norm + task head, repeated L times. A dashed line links the HSA block to a blue callout. The callout reads 'Query selects a boundary direction, q_i → v_i', followed by the Busemann score s_ij = −τ B_vi(k_j). Orange and blue separate the two geometric notions, and the eye goes first to the disk.
caption: BusemannFormer overview. (a) In the Poincaré disk H2, HSA favors directionally aligned k2 over nearby k1. Orange/blue curves mark equal hyperbolic distance/Busemann depth. (b) The hyperbolic Transformer uses HSA: each query selects a boundary direction and scores keys by Busemann depth; ⊕denotes spatial addition and lift.
abstract: Hyperbolic neural networks excel on hierarchical graph data, yet existing hyperbolic Transformers largely adapt conventional attention without explicitly exploiting the ideal boundary, a geometric structure closely tied to tree hierarchy. We propose Horospherical Self-Attention (HSA): each query selects an ideal-boundary direction and scores keys by their Busemann depth along that direction, yielding a token-to-token hyperbolic attention kernel. We establish a flat-limit connection to dot-product attention, characterize score level sets as horospheres, and bound key-side gradients. HSA is integrated into BusemannFormer, a fully hyperbolic graph Transformer, with a log-depth variant that uses query depth to modulate attention concentration. We further introduce a finite-boundary-dictionary extension supporting linear-complexity global attention. Experiments on hierarchical and citation graphs show that BusemannFormer-LD outperforms the evaluated baselines on several node-classification benchmarks and achieves competitive performance across diverse graph structures.
